Definition: from G2932; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal:--beast.
BiblicalUsage: The beast here is the domestic animal, the creature a man owns and rides. In Acts 23:24 the chief captain orders them to "provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on," and in 1 Corinthians 15:39 Paul says "all flesh is not the same flesh," but there is one kind of flesh of men, another of beasts.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word keeps the distinction plain: man and beast are both flesh, but they are not the same flesh, and God made them different on purpose.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
